extracted.intended_audience: pre-service middle grades mathematics teachers and mathematics education faculty/program developers
extracted.subtask_description: Description of an undergraduate cohort-based middle grades mathematics teacher preparation program (Georgia College & State University), including admission requirements, course structure, field experiences, course goals, assessment practices, and certification standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission criteria for middle grades program
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for admission include completing all areas of the Core curriculum (including two entry-level mathematics courses) with a minimum 2.5 GPA; completing six pre-education courses (three introductory education and three content-related); passing the reading and writing subtests of the Georgia Regents’ Examination; passing the GACE I Academic Skills Assessment (or equivalent SAT/ACT scores); submitting three acceptable letters of recommendation; and completing a formal interview with program representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit, required checkpoints for students applying in the spring of their sophomore year. Admission signals an expectation of intensive commitment to the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student time and commitment expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Students admitted are expected to commit approximately 40 hours each week to taking classes and their field placements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students receive a Student Handbook detailing expectations and decision-point requirements; admission implies understanding and acceptance of this weekly time commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program sequence and field placement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sequence spans freshman through senior years with progressively intensive field placements: junior-year placements in four different school settings (mostly rural) with 16–20 hours per week in a mathematics classroom; senior-year single placement with pre-planning and a minimum of three weeks of full-time teaching. By graduation, students should have over 1000 hours of classroom experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placements are structured to provide varied classroom contexts and practical application of theory. Host teachers are selected to supervise candidates and facilitate application of classroom learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort model and collaborative structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Students enter cohort groups of 15–25 in their junior year and take most professional courses together, with occasional sub-cohorts for content concentrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cohort model is intended to enhance collaboration, development of professional dispositions, and consistent evaluation standards across the program; it also fosters peer support that mirrors collaborative work in schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics concentration coursework requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Middle grades majors with a mathematics concentration must successfully complete four mathematics courses and three mathematics education courses; elementary preparation requires two content courses and three math education courses. Entry-level course choices include mathematical modeling, precalculus, survey of calculus, calculus, linear algebra, or elementary statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course selection is made in consultation with an advisor and based on student background and interests; elementary statistics is encouraged due to its relevance in middle grades curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals and practices for Concepts in Geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: The geometry course aims to develop a conceptual understanding of Euclidean geometry and measurement (perimeter, area, volume), covering classes of figures, symmetry, transformations, similarity/congruence, and constructions. Frequent use of The Geometer’s Sketchpad (GSP) as an exploration tool and hands-on manipulatives (patty paper, pattern blocks, pentominoes, tiles, D-Sticks) is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students are guided with leading questions and organizational supports early in the semester, with scaffolding reduced over time so students take more independent exploratory responsibility (construct vs. draw distinction emphasized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals and practices for Concepts in Algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: The algebra course focuses on moving beyond procedural algebra to understanding patterns, functions, modeling, and structural properties of the number system. Emphasis is placed on algebraic reasoning via pattern generalization, visual patterns, use of manipulatives (toothpicks, tiles, counters), conjecture formation, and verification/proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities are designed to broaden students' understanding of functions and modeling, connect algebra to geometry and data, and encourage students to verify results rather than accept assertions by authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem write-up assessment rubric (Polya-based four-section write-up)
rubrics_metrics.description: Student problem write-ups are organized into four sections aligned with Pólya’s heuristic: (1) Problem Set Up — state and paraphrase the problem; (2) Plans to Solve/Investigate — discuss connections, consider simpler related problems, and represent the problem (algebraically, graphically, numerically, and/or verbally); (3) Investigation/Exploration — detail how the problem was solved, showing multiple representations with at least one visual and using technology/manipulatives for exploration; (4) Extension — reflect on findings, ensure solution makes sense, and generalize or prove conjectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems are defined as tasks without a set procedure; students are expected to follow the sections, include at least one visual representation, and use technology/manipulatives as exploratory tools (not merely to display final answers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of inquiry-based, student-centered instructional strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses emphasize inquiry-based activities, exploration, manipulatives, technology, mathematical communication (oral and written), focus on conceptual 'why' not just 'how', reading current research, and interdisciplinary connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional choices (tasks, activities, technology) are selected to enhance both content knowledge and pedagogical content knowledge. Examples include the chords-of-a-circle inductive/counterexample activity and the Incomplete Boat GSP task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and certification standards alignment (GSTEP / AMLE / INTASC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program uses the Georgia Systematic Teacher Education Program (GSTEP) Framework for Accomplished Teaching and AMLE (formerly NMSA) standards for Initial Middle Level Teacher Preparation to assess candidates. These frameworks (aligned with INTASC principles) specify detailed knowledge, dispositions, and performances required of candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates must satisfy each standard as determined by faculty across areas such as student development (young adolescents), learning environments/philosophy and school organization, curriculum/instruction/assessment, family and community involvement, and professional roles. Satisfying these standards plus passing the GACE II content exam are prerequisites for recommendation for state certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program success/outcome metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Program effectiveness is evaluated using outcome metrics such as state certification test pass rates, principal/employer evaluations of beginning teachers, and teacher retention rates over multiple years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: consistently 100% pass rate on state certification test in two content-area concentrations; a 2003 administrator survey where 91% of beginning teachers were rated 'good' or 'excellent'; retention statistics showing high percentages of graduates remaining in education over several years. These metrics are used as evidence of program quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field supervision and host teacher role
rubrics_metrics.description: Students spend supervised hours in classrooms under the guidance of selected host teachers who supervise and mentor teacher candidates during field placements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host teachers are chosen to support the students' practical experiences; placements occur in varied school contexts to broaden candidate experience and support application of theory to practice.
